experiment: selected update100 small-step control on frozen diff-shape factorial audit
assessment_method: Read all16 exact raw responses against all8 predeclared complete C fixtures; assessed meaning separately from JSON/schema acceptance. No generation or model arithmetic was run for this assessment.
deletion_hypothesis_conclusions: The original training-template observation is reproducible: six pure-deletion concern cases win66582, while all fourteen concerns containing additions win788. All40 replayed outputs and actual first IDs agree with the preserved archive and teacher argmax.
In the expanded factorial fixtures, natural generation returns the same fenced empty array for all8 cases: four clean cases correct, four harmful cases missed.

After the identical shared prefix, all8 fixtures start with788, including both harmful pure deletions. The original pure-deletion-to66582 pattern therefore depends on the original prompt context and does not hold across these expanded contexts.

Within each fixed context, replacing the deleted guard with (void)0 leaves the first generated ID unchanged. Retaining another working guard also leaves that ID unchanged. The controlled shape and harm contrasts produce no first-token separation.

All8 shared responses copy changed-line text into attempted findings. Six are JSON arrays of strings; the two NULL-guard replacement responses add an extra closing brace. Parsed presence stays null for these two malformed responses.

The shared responses explain neither allocation-failure dereference nor permission bypass. They also flag the four clean redundant-guard changes. The observed failure is changed-line copying without checking whether an effective guard remains.

The harmful pure-deletion audit cases expand the original partial snippets into full functions, add explicit no-other-check context and change line coordinates. Their different token route localizes sensitivity to that combined context change; the within-audit factorial comparisons isolate no-op replacement and presence of the earlier effective guard.
